clue.text: Keep using unusual dialect

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of the following word are set out in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A linguist relies on an odd regional dialect to get by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the noun: a castle's stronghold. 'unusual' rearranges DIALECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central tower of a castle, much like a stronghold or fortress.

clue.text: With passion rising during exam, see red

indicators.note: during says one piece lies within another

parts.note: the CSE was a former British school exam, the Certificate of Secondary Education

indicators.note: rising in a down clue says the word is read upwards

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: A student gets furious during an exam and sees red.
explanation.walkthrough: The CSE was a British school-leaving exam, the Certificate of Secondary Education. 'rising' turns the passion word upwards, and 'during' sets it inside the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a bright cherry colour, a shade of red.

clue.text: Continent with balmy climate

definitions.meaning: mild in weather, neither very hot nor very cold

explanation.surface: A continent enjoys a mild climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continent' looks like a landmass, but here it is the adjective meaning self-controlled.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both moderate in habits and having a mild climate.

clue.text: A lot of people in the police turn up full of energy

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue says the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
in says one piece lies within the other

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police
many means a lot of people

explanation.surface: Crowds of police appear, bursting with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' sounds like arriving, but reverses CIMANYD, giving DYNAMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic means vigorous and energetic.

clue.text: Voicing harsh criticism about races just before retiring

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: lashing is a fierce verbal attack
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: Someone slates the racing just before going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle races. 'Voicing' looks like speaking aloud but is part of the phrase for a verbal attack; 'about' wraps it around the races.
explanation.definitionFit: The last thing at night is what one does just before going to bed.

clue.text: Listen to pop singer in a dressing-gown

indicators.note: Listen to tells us we want a word that matches another when spoken

parts.note: a rapper is a performer of hip-hop, a kind of pop singer

explanation.surface: A music fan hears a pop star performing while wearing a bathrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen to' says the word for a pop singer, RAPPER, is matched in speech by a word with a silent W.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is a loose robe or gown worn indoors, so it can name a dressing-gown.

clue.text: Wife needs assistance to give birth

parts.note: help means assistance

explanation.surface: A wife needs help to deliver her baby.
explanation.definitionFit: To whelp is to give birth to puppies or cubs.

clue.text: Unhappily married? You need a lover

indicators.note: Unhappily tells us the letters of the word next to it are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A spouse in a bad marriage is told to find a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is someone romantically attracted to another, a suitor or lover.

clue.text: See father with fruit

parts.note: the Pope, father of the Holy See, is papa in Italian

explanation.surface: A child is told to look at Dad with some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction to look, but means the Holy See, whose father is the Pope, or PAPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaw is another name for the papaya, a tropical fruit.

clue.text: One writing in newspaper on drink

parts.note: re means on, in the sense of concerning
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A journalist writes about drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter is a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter writes news stories for a paper.

clue.text: About cars engineer becomes nostalgic

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Minis are small British cars
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: Thinking about old cars makes an engineer misty-eyed for the past.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is a civil engineer; the Mini is a classic small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall the past fondly, which is what someone growing nostalgic does.

clue.text: Dispose of worthless purchase after a short time

indicators.note: after says the purchase comes behind the short time in the answer

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a short time
to be sold a pup is to buy something worthless

explanation.surface: Someone wants to get rid of a dud buy soon after acquiring it.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'sold a pup' is a British idiom for being swindled into a worthless purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to deal with or eliminate remaining things, so it can mean dispose of.

clue.text: Impetus uniting second eleven, perhaps

parts.note: an eleven, as in cricket or football, is an example of a team

explanation.surface: A coach seeks something to drive on the reserve side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second eleven' reads as the reserve side, but splits into S and an example of a TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is driving force or momentum, as in gathering steam, so it means impetus.

clue.text: People of the highest standing, such as da Vinci?

definitions.meaning: the upper class, those of the best social rank
a supreme draughtsman, playfully read as a drawer of the first rank

explanation.surface: Society's elite are compared to a great Renaissance artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the phrase into 'top' and 'drawer', one who draws, which Leonardo da Vinci famously did.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the highest social class; read literally it praises a superb draughtsman.

clue.text: Game in which cut receives ointment without a name

indicators.note: receives says one piece is taken into the middle of another

parts.note: to abridge a text is to cut it

indicators.note: without says a letter is taken away from the word for ointment

parts.note: unction is an ointment, an oil for anointing

explanation.surface: In some sport, a wound has balm applied without anyone being named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a wound but means shorten a text. 'without' drops the name's letter from the ointment, and 'receives' places what is left after the first letter of the cut word.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction bridge is a card game, a forerunner of contract bridge.

clue.text: Card-playing can result in beggary for him

definitions.text: Card-playing can result in beggary for him

parts.words: Card-playing can result in beggary for him
parts.note: alludes to the children's card game Beggar-my-..., in which the person next door is the one made poor

explanation.surface: A gambler's cards could leave him a pauper.
explanation.walkthrough: Beggar-my-neighbour is a simple card game; the clue reads its name literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is the person living next door, named in the game's title.

clue.text: Forgo party and comedian entertaining a thousand

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: entertaining says the comedian holds the thousand inside

parts.note: a wit is a clever, funny person
thou is slang for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone skips a party where a comic is hosting a thousand guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comedian' points to a witty person rather than a stand-up. 'entertaining' sets the slang thousand inside that word, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To do without something is to forgo it.

clue.text: Evening up weight, one not heavy enough

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
light means under the required weight

explanation.surface: Someone evens up the weights, as one is too light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening up' reads as levelling, but 'Evening' is the definition and 'up' reverses WT.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim time after sunset, early evening.

clue.text: Sound often heard from radar equipment as little bat comes round tree

indicators.note: comes round says the two outer pieces surround the radar sound

parts.note: wee is a Scottish word for little
cricket bats are made of willow, so willow can stand for a bat

parts.words: Sound often heard from radar equipment
parts.note: a ping is the short pulse sound of sonar or radar

explanation.surface: A radar beeps as a small flying bat circles a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bat' suggests the flying mammal, but it is a cricket bat, made from willow. 'comes round' puts the radar sound between the little and bat pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The weeping willow is a tree with long drooping branches.

clue.text: Levantine is an artist — and a priest

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Eli was a priest in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone from the eastern Mediterranean is both a painter and a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is a Royal Academician; Eli is the priest who raised Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel lies in the Levant, so an Israeli is a Levantine person.

clue.text: Imbecile gets involved in a cult

indicators.note: gets involved says the letters of the phrase are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool joins a cult.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are insults for a person thought foolish or mad.

clue.text: Religious book confused many in the House of Lords

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters go inside the abbreviation

parts.note: HL is the abbreviation for the House of Lords

indicators.note: confused says the letters of the word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A prayer book bewilders many peers in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges the letters of many, and 'in' puts the result between the two letters standing for the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a book of hymns used in worship.

clue.text: After onset of labour, any birth can turn into confusing process

indicators.note: onset of picks the opening letter of the next word
can turn into says the letters of the phrase change into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Once labour begins, any delivery can become a bewildering ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can turn into' rearranges ANY BIRTH into ABYRINTH, after L from 'onset of labour'.
explanation.definitionFit: A labyrinth is a maze, figuratively any intricate, bewildering procedure.

clue.text: Some Africans put a curse on Equity, for instance

indicators.note: on in a down clue says the curse sits above the union

parts.note: a ban can be a curse, as in an anathema
Equity is the British actors' union, an example of a trade union, TU

explanation.surface: Some Africans curse the actors' union.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the British actors' trade union. 'on' in a down clue puts BAN above TU.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu are a large family of peoples of central and southern Africa.

clue.text: Noisy piece, the follow-up to 16

indicators.note: Noisy says we take a word as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A loud item comes after the previous answer.
explanation.walkthrough: A chess knight is spoken without its K. 16 down is TWILIGHT, which night follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Night falls after twilight, so it follows the answer to 16.

clue.text: Like Brazil's 19

definitions.meaning: resembling a Brazil, a kind of nut
the answer to 19 down, meaning mad or crazy

explanation.surface: Something resembles a Brazilian's madman.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brazil is a nut, so something like it tastes of nuts; 19 down is LUNATIC, and the word also means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means tasting of nuts and, informally, crazy, matching both a Brazil nut and a madman.

clue.text: Information concerning artistic style

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means concerning

explanation.surface: Details are given about a particular art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as in 'the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or style of artistic work, such as a type of painting or literature.

clue.text: Empty place where entertainer has time to get into dress

indicators.note: to get into says pieces go inside the dress word

parts.note: a gown is a dress
a host entertains guests

explanation.surface: In an empty theatre, a performer is given time to change outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get into' puts the entertainer and the time letter inside the dress, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost town is a deserted settlement, an empty place.

clue.text: He travels for pleasure, as far as historic city, first

parts.note: to can mean as far as, as in up to the gate
Ur is an ancient city of Mesopotamia
1st, written as ist with I for one, means first

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker travels as far as an ancient city before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' becomes 1ST, read as IST with the figure 1 as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone who travels for pleasure or sightseeing.

clue.text: Performance from retired principal at ice rink

indicators.note: retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the answer's letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A retired head of a skating rink puts on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's hidden run lacked its indicator: 'from' signals the letters lie within the phrase, and 'retired' turns LATICER around.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance, often by a soloist.
